sanskrit_shloka:
जनक उवाच ॥
हन्तात्मज्ञानस्य धीरस्य खेलतो भोगलीलया ।
न हि संसारवाहीकैर्मूढैः सह समानता ॥ ४-१॥
translation: Janaka said: Ah! The wise one, playing in the līlā of enjoyment born of Self-knowledge, can never be equal to the fools carried along by the currents of saṃsāra.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Janaka said: Ah! The wise one, playing in the līlā of enjoyment born of Self-knowledge, can never be equal to the fools carried along by the currents of saṃsāra.

commentary_faqs.question: How does a Self-realized person view virtue and sin?
commentary_faqs.answer: According to Verse 3, the Knower of the Self is internally untouched by virtue or sin, just as the vast space (akasha) remains unaffected by the presence of smoke.

commentary_faqs.question: Why is the sage described as fearless in this chapter?
commentary_faqs.answer: Fear arises from the perception of duality or 'the other'. By realizing the non-dual Self as the Lord of the universe, the sage sees nothing separate from themselves, thus eliminating all fear.

commentary_faqs.question: How does the sage's joy compare to that of the gods?
commentary_faqs.answer: Janaka states that the yogi established in the Self does not experience worldly joy from the very positions and pleasures that even Indra and other gods desperately seek.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत् पदं प्रेप्सवो दीनाः शक्राद्याः सर्वदेवताः ।
अहो तत्र स्थितो योगी न हर्षमुपगच्छति ॥ ४-२॥
translation: The yogi established in that state sought humbly by Indra and all the gods—ah, wonder!—does not fall into elation over worldly pleasures.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The yogi established in that state sought humbly by Indra and all the gods—ah, wonder!—does not fall into elation over worldly pleasures.

sanskrit_shloka:
तज्ज्ञस्य पुण्यपापाभ्यां स्पर्शो ह्यन्तर्न जायते ।
न ह्याकाशस्य धूमेन दृश्यमानापि सङ्गतिः ॥ ४-३॥
translation: For the knower of the Self, no inner contact with merit or sin arises; just as space is not joined to smoke, even though smoke appears within it.

sanskrit_shloka:
आत्मैवेदं जगत्सर्वं ज्ञातं येन महात्मना ।
यदृच्छया वर्तमानं तं निषेद्धुं क्षमेत कः ॥ ४-४॥
translation: Who could restrain or negate the great soul who has known this entire world to be the Self alone, and who abides spontaneously as things arise?

sanskrit_shloka:
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्ते भूतग्रामे चतुर्विधे ।
विज्ञस्यैव हि सामर्थ्यमिच्छानिच्छाविवर्जने ॥ ४-५॥
translation: Among all beings of the four kinds, from Brahmā down to the smallest blade of grass, only the knower has the power to be free from desire and aversion.

translations.author: English Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
आत्मानमद्वयं कश्चिज्जानाति जगदीश्वरम् ।
यद् वेत्ति तत्स कुरुते न भयं तस्य कुत्रचित् ॥ ४-६॥
translation: One who knows the non-dual Self as the Lord of the universe acts in accord with that knowing; for such a one, there is no fear anywhere.
